note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). prepare/teardown run on the laptop, not recorded; commands are typed and run for real. Prepare statements run in one PowerShell session with the episode folder as current directory; variables do not survive into the screens, so each screen re-derives what it needs.
prepare: # owner, once: Docker Desktop running, Node.js, Postman desktop app (free plan) signed in with the lab labadmin mailbox, gh auth login
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\work | Out-Null; Remove-Item C:\work\orders-app-api-tests -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
git init -q -b main; git config core.autocrlf false; git config user.name 'Alex Demo'; git config user.email 'alex.demo@contoso.com'
git add -A; git commit -q -m 'chore: import the orders API with its Postman collection'
docker rm -f orders-api 2>$null; docker run --rm -d --name orders-api -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 contoso/orders-api:dev

screens.name: import
steps: Create a new empty workspace named orders-api-demo
Show the import options (collection only vs. specification with a collection) and choose collection
Show the generated collection: folders and requests for /healthz, /orders, /orders/{id}
Open the POST /orders request and one saved example response; open its Tests tab: empty (this is the point of the scene)
Then import orders-api.postman_collection.json and environments\local.postman_environment.json (as a second collection named 'Contoso Orders API')
mask: Postman account name and e-mail, workspace owner
Windows user name in file pickers

screens.name: runner
steps: Select the environment 'local' (baseUrl http://localhost:8080); the API container is running (prepare)
Open Contoso Orders API > Orders > Create order; show the Pre-request Script and Tests tabs and press Send: Test Results shows 5 passing
Open the collection's Variables tab: orderId and createdOrder are filled
Run collection (Runner): tick Health, Orders, Validation (Data-driven off), Run; all requests green and the assertion totals (31 with expectedVersion empty)
Optional: run Data-driven with data\invalid-orders.json (6 iterations); if Postman asks for a paid plan skip it (the regression screen shows the same run in the terminal). Do not buy a plan.
mask: Postman account name and e-mail, workspace owner
Windows user name in file pickers

screens.name: regression
prepare: [IO.File]::WriteAllText('C:\work\bin\dotnet-tree', ((@('#!/bin/bash', '# DOTNET for scripts/run-api-tests.sh on Windows: Git Bash''s kill ends only "dotnet run", not the API it started (which then keeps bin locked for the next run); this ends the whole process tree', 'dotnet "$@" &', 'child=$!', 'trap ''w=$(cat /proc/$child/winpid 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$w" ] && taskkill //F //T //PID "$w" >/dev/null 2>&1; kill "$child" 2>/dev/null; exit 143'' TERM INT HUP', 'wait "$child"') -join "`n") + "`n")); $env:DOTNET = 'dotnet-tree'
commands: # break the page-size cap on purpose
screens.note: First run: both Newman tables green, gate lines 'junit-main.xml: 31 passed' and 'junit-data.xml: 24 passed', exit code 0. Second run: exactly one failure 'cap: asking for 500 returns at most 100', gate line with the failed assertion, exit code 1. The script picks a free port, so the container on 8080 does not conflict.

screens.name: ci
prepare: git add -A; git commit -m 'docs: add a changelog'; git push -u origin test/show-the-gates
gh run watch (gh run list --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId') --exit-status
steps: Open the pull request 'docs: add a changelog' and its Checks tab, the workflow run 'api-tests'
Step 'Lint the collection and the environments': '10 requests, 1 environment(s): no problems'
Step 'Every documented operation and response has a test': the 4-row table, all ok, '4 operations, all covered'
Step 'Run the collection against the API built from this commit': Newman output; the gate lines show 32 and 24 (CI sets EXPECTED_VERSION)
Run Summary: the artifact api-test-results (junit-main.xml, junit-data.xml)
mask: GitHub account name if it is not the public lab account

teardown: docker rm -f orders-api 2>$null; docker rmi contoso/orders-api:dev
# owner: Postman > delete the workspace orders-api-demo (collections and environment inside); the free account stays
$owner = gh api user --jq .login; if (gh repo view "$owner/orders-app-api-tests" --json name 2>$null) { gh repo delete "$owner/orders-app-api-tests" --yes }
prepare_local: Use-DotNetSdk -Channel 10.0   # kit helper: uses the installed .NET 10 SDK, else installs it into C:\MGLab\dotnet (no admin)

[IO.File]::WriteAllText('C:\work\bin\dotnet-tree', ((@('#!/bin/bash', '# DOTNET for scripts/run-api-tests.sh on Windows: Git Bash''s kill ends only "dotnet run", not the API it started (which then keeps bin locked for the next run); this ends the whole process tree', 'dotnet "$@" &', 'child=$!', 'trap ''w=$(cat /proc/$child/winpid 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$w" ] && taskkill //F //T //PID "$w" >/dev/null 2>&1; kill "$child" 2>/dev/null; exit 143'' TERM INT HUP', 'wait "$child"') -join "`n") + "`n")); $env:DOTNET = 'dotnet-tree'

Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq 'Contoso.Orders.Api.exe' -or ($_.Name -eq 'dotnet.exe' -and $_.CommandLine -like '*Contoso.Orders.Api*') } | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }   # no orders API left running (it would lock bin)
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force C:\work | Out-Null; Remove-Item C:\work\orders-app-api-tests -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
git init -q -b main; git config core.autocrlf false; git config user.name 'Alex Demo'; git config user.email 'alex.demo@contoso.com'
git add -A; git commit -q -m 'chore: import the orders API with its Postman collection'

bash scripts/run-api-tests.sh | Out-Null; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { "warm-up run exit code $LASTEXITCODE (a cold first run can miss the 2000 ms check): once more" | Out-Host; bash scripts/run-api-tests.sh | Out-Null }; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "off-camera warm-up of scripts/run-api-tests.sh failed (exit $LASTEXITCODE): the on-camera run would not be green" }   # off-camera warm-up run

Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.Name -eq 'Contoso.Orders.Api.exe' -or ($_.Name -eq 'dotnet.exe' -and $_.CommandLine -like '*Contoso.Orders.Api*') } | ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }   # no orders API left running (it would lock bin)
